key_insight: (MPO)^2 learns multivariate polynomial models with matrix product operators, making polynomial function approximation more expressive and feature-order independent.
engineering_relevance: It offers a compact way to model complex input-output relationships for machine learning and signal processing without the exponential cost of full polynomial tensors.
method: Learns MPO-based feature embeddings to compress polynomial representations.
Uses compact polynomial weight tensors with structured operators such as projections, convolutions, and masks.
Avoids feature-order dependence seen in tensor-train formulations while improving expressivity over CP-based models.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports improvements over existing tensor-decomposition polynomial models on regression and classification benchmarks.
watch_item: Performance may depend on careful MPO/weight-tensor design and implementation details for structured operators and symmetry constraints.
paper_title: (MPO)$^2$: Multivariate Polynomial Optimization based on Matrix Product Operators
